findings.ref: human-copy/plugins/sdd-quality-loop/scripts/resolve-project-context.py -- _pre_publication_recheck plus main()'s five new step-13 except clauses (CanonicalizerFailed / CanonicalizerOutputMalformed / AffectedComponentResolutionFailed / DependencySubprocessFailed / DependencyOutputMalformed); reports/implementation/epic-193-a5-capability-resolver/T-004.md "Fourth Pass -- Mutation Kills", Finding 3
findings.note: The Finding-3 remediation ships with zero test coverage in a Required Workflow: tdd, Risk: high task. The report discloses it honestly: "re-wrapping _pre_publication_recheck's own three dependency calls back into SnapshotGenerationMismatch is a behavior-preserving revert with no fixture regression on its own ... this finding's own fix has no dedicated fixture ... not a mutant kill." The change is observable contract behavior -- which REQ-002 id and which canonical AC-014 detail sentence a caller sees when a recheck-internal subprocess fails -- and it introduced five new detail sentences that no assertion in tests/resolve-project-context-block-check.py can ever exercise (run_t004_case's five cases are lite-check-source-undefined, output-schema-validation-failed-{evidence,artifact}, snapshot-generation-mismatch, contract-discovery-failed-governing-schema; the snapshot fixture's stub exits 0 with a differing digest, never fails to run). A regression that re-collapses these back to snapshot-generation-mismatch is silently green. This driver's own precedent contradicts accepting the gap: the immediately prior panel round added resolve-component-paths-launch-failed and registry-discovery-unimportable fixtures for exactly this class of previously-untested dependency-failure path.

Step 12's local draft-07 engine silently no-ops on every keyword it does not implement, and nothing asserts its keyword set covers the four governing schemas. Two consecutive panel rounds each found one instance of this class (`not`, then `minimum`) and each was closed keyword-by-keyword; the class itself is still open -- allOf, anyOf, maximum, exclusiveMinimum/Maximum, maxLength, maxItems, patternProperties, dependencies, contains, and array-form `items` (tuple validation) all fall through with no diagnostic, so an instance the governing schema forbids passes the self-check. That is precisely the failure the step exists to prevent ("a schema-conformance defect in this feature's own assembly logic must never reach a live path"). The risk is concrete rather than theoretical: two of the four governing schemas the engine must satisfy (contracts/resolver-evidence.schema.json and contracts/facet-manifest.schema.json) are absent from this bundle, so the engine's adequacy against them is unverifiable here, and the report states Epic A4's real context-projection schema is fully typed while the exercised stand-in is a deliberately looser partial transcription (projectedComponent: additionalProperties: true). A closure assertion -- enumerate every keyword appearing in the four discovered governing schema documents and fail if _draft7_validate does not implement it -- would kill the whole class in one check; without it each round can only find one more instance.

The Context Projection is self-validated on BOTH tracks, but design.md step 10b states that on the Lite track "no facet-manifest.yaml and no project-context.resolved.json are staged or written", and step 12's scope is "every artifact staged through steps 3/10/11". A Lite resolve can therefore Block with `output-schema-validation-failed: the staged context-projection artifact failed ...` for an artifact the design places outside that track's staged set. The drift is fail-closed rather than fail-open, and no T-004 fixture reaches step 12 on the Lite track at all (all four Block fixtures are Full-track or Block before step 12, as Specification Differences item 3 discloses), so the Lite step-12 path is entirely unexercised.

Stale declarations left standing against current behavior. Item 4 asserts "_write_evidence/_block (T-002-owned) is reused unchanged for all three of this task's own new Block records -- none of them adds context_binding/resolver to the written Evidence ... a deliberate, conservative choice"; the Fourth Pass reversed exactly that, and the shipped code threads context_binding/resolver into four late-Block call sites. Item 3 likewise still says "all three of this task's own new Block fixtures" where run_t004_case now carries five case names. Neither item is struck or annotated as superseded, so the report's own normative section contradicts the code a reader is asked to verify against it.
